title: Product sync — Q4 firmware

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Alright, let's get going.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Thanks all for making time this afternoon, I know it's been a heavy week.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Agenda's the usual, release scope, bug backlog, field feedback, then rev C hardware status, and we'll close with action items.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Sounds good.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Should I start with scope since that's probably the longest conversation?

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Yeah, go ahead.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: For the Q4 firmware release on the Vantage line, we've got four things in scope right now, the low-power sleep mode work, the calibration table patch for the humidity drift issue, the Bluetooth low energy diagnostic mode, and the cloud connectivity retry logic.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Tomas is owning sleep mode, I'm owning the calibration patch, and Inès has been helping with the BLE diagnostic mode from the hardware side.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: And the cloud connectivity piece, who's on that?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Nobody yet, honestly, it's been sitting in the backlog.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: It's a smaller change, retrying failed uploads with exponential backoff instead of the current fixed one-minute retry, but it's not assigned.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Let's talk about whether it needs to be in this release at all, or if it can slip to the point release after.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: I'd vote slip it.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: It's not customer facing in the sense that units still upload eventually, they just retry more slowly than ideal.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Sleep mode and the calibration fix are both more urgent.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: I agree, and honestly the connectivity code touches the same buffer management as the BLE diagnostic mode, I'd rather not have two people modifying that path in the same release cycle.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Before we defer it entirely, what's the actual customer impact of the current fixed retry, does anyone have numbers?

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Roughly, if a unit loses connectivity for under a minute it's invisible, no data loss.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Between one and six minutes it retries on the fixed schedule and usually catches up fine.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Past about six minutes of outage it starts dropping the oldest buffered readings, same buffer limit issue Northfield ran into, so the two problems are actually related.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Interesting, so exponential backoff alone doesn't fix the data loss, it just changes how aggressively we retry.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Right, the backoff change is really about not hammering the server with retries when connectivity's flaky, it's a server load and battery consideration more than a data integrity one.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: The buffer size is the actual fix for data loss.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: Which argues for doing them together in the Q1 session rather than splitting the backoff logic out now and revisiting the buffer separately later.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Agreed, that's a better argument for deferring both together than I had a minute ago.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Okay, let's defer cloud connectivity to the point release after freeze, I'll note that as a decision, and we'll scope it jointly with the buffer work in Q1.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Maya, keep going with sleep mode and the calibration patch.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Right, sleep mode.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Tomas, you want to give the status since you're closer to it than me at this point?

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Sure.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: It's mostly done, the state machine rewrite is in, the tricky part was handling wake sources correctly during an in-progress firmware update, we don't want a unit to go to sleep mid-flash and brick itself.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: That's tested now against six different wake scenarios.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: What's left is characterizing the actual current draw across temperature, and that's blocked on the rev C boards.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Right, we'll get to rev C in a minute.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: How confident are you in the current draw numbers you do have, from the rev B units?

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Reasonably confident, we're seeing about forty microamps in deep sleep, down from around three hundred on the current shipping firmware.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: That's roughly a seven times improvement, which was the target Maya and I set back in July.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: That's a great number, that alone is worth a customer email once it ships.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Maya, calibration patch status?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Good progress.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I mentioned this in our 1:1 earlier this week, we found the root cause of a slow drift on the humidity channel, it was the reference temperature compensation table being built off the old thermistor curve instead of the one used on the rev B parts.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I've got a corrected table from bench data on twelve units, and we're running a seventy-two hour soak test now at three humidity setpoints to validate it before shipping.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: And that's the one affecting Solenne Biolabs?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Right, they flagged drift over a forty-eight hour unattended run in one of their incubators.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I've already let their support contact know we're targeting a patch within two weeks, ahead of the main Q4 release.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: Is there a hardware angle to that at all, or is it purely a firmware lookup table issue?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Purely firmware as far as I can tell, the sensor itself reads correctly, it's our interpretation of the reading that was off.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: If the soak test comes back clean I don't think we need any hardware changes.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Walk me through the math a bit, just so I can explain it if a customer asks.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Why does a small thermistor curve error turn into a visible drift over time instead of just a constant offset?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Good question, it's because the compensation is nonlinear and temperature dependent, so the error isn't constant, it grows as the unit's internal temperature drifts over a long run, mostly from the sensor's own self-heating as it takes more readings.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Early in a run the error's negligible, under a tenth of a percent, but after forty-plus hours of continuous logging it can compound to something noticeable.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: And the corrected table just uses the right reference curve for the actual thermistor part on rev B boards.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Exactly, once we swap in the curve that matches the part that's actually populated, the compensation stays accurate regardless of how long the unit's been running, because we're compensating against real physical behavior instead of an approximation for a different part.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: Is there a way to detect this kind of mismatch automatically in the future, so it doesn't take a customer complaint to surface it?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: That's actually a good idea for the Q1 documentation sprint, a sanity check at first boot that cross-references the reported part ID against the loaded compensation table and warns if they don't match.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I'll add it to my list.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: Good, one less thing on my plate this month.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Speaking of your plate, Inès, how's the BLE diagnostic mode coming along?

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: It's functional, we can pull live signal strength and packet loss stats over BLE now without needing a USB connection, which the field techs have been asking for since the spring.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: The remaining work is mostly UI polish on the companion app side, which isn't really my lane, that's on the mobile team.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Right, I need to sync with them separately on timeline, I'll take that as an action item.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Is there anything on the security side worth flagging for the BLE mode, since it's a new attack surface once units are broadcasting diagnostics over the air?

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: We thought about that.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: The diagnostic broadcast requires a pairing code printed on the unit's underside, so it's not open to anyone walking by with a phone, and it only transmits signal strength and packet loss counters, nothing about the actual sensor readings or any customer data.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Good, that was going to be my next question, whether any measurement data could leak.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Sounds like we're fine there.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: Right, and the pairing code rotates on power cycle too, so it's not even a fixed secret sitting on a public-facing label indefinitely.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: One thing worth flagging though, we found a connector debounce issue on three units out of the last batch of fifty, the USB-C port intermittently disconnects if you wiggle the cable at a certain angle.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: It's not new firmware related, but I wanted it on the radar before the release goes out, since support will get calls about it either way.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: How serious is it, mechanical or is there a firmware-side mitigation?

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: Mostly mechanical, the connector's tolerance stack is a little loose on that batch, but we can improve the debounce timing in firmware to mask most of the symptom, treat brief disconnects under fifty milliseconds as noise instead of a real unplug event.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: I can add that debounce change, it's a small diff, maybe half a day.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Let's do that, add it to the release scope, small but worth it.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Okay, let's move to the general bug backlog, what else came out of grooming?

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: The Bluetooth reconnect loop bug is still open, the one where a unit walked more than thirty meters from the base station won't reconnect cleanly without a power cycle.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: We triaged it as low priority at standup this morning since it's an edge case, but wanted to mention it here too in case anyone disagrees.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: No, I agree it's low priority, let's leave it in the backlog for now, it's not worth delaying the release over.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: There were also a couple of smaller UI string issues on the local display, wrong unit label on the pressure reading when the device is set to metric versus imperial.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Small fix, already in progress.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: And one more, we noticed the fault-code table Inès added last sprint pushed flash usage up to about ninety-one percent on the C-series board, which is getting close to the ceiling.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Tomas mentioned that at standup too, what's the plan there?

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: For now, I'm dropping the diagnostic logging changes I had planned for this release, that buys us some headroom, and Greta's stripping verbose calibration strings from the release build.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Between the two we should be back under eighty-five percent.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Okay, that should hold us for this cycle, but let's put a longer-term flash budget review on the radar for Q1, before Aegis firmware starts sharing space on any common code paths.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Agreed, that's worth its own session, not something to rush through here.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Noted, I'll set that up separately.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Let's talk field feedback more broadly, beyond the Solenne drift issue, what else are we hearing?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Northfield Analytical sent over some notes from their pilot, mostly positive.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Their main ask is a longer local data buffer, right now if a unit loses connectivity for more than six hours it starts dropping the oldest readings, and they'd like at least twenty-four hours of buffer for their remote field sites.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Is that feasible for this release, or is that its own project?

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: It's mostly a memory allocation question, we have the flash headroom concern we just talked about, so probably not this release, but I can scope it properly for Q1 alongside the flash budget review.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Let's fold it into that same Q1 session then, they're related.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: What's Northfield's timeline expectation on this, are they patient or is this becoming a churn risk?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: They've been patient so far, they mentioned it more as a wishlist item than a complaint, but their pilot converts to a paid contract at the end of Q1, so I'd like to have at least a committed timeline to share with them before that renewal conversation, even if the actual fix lands after.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Good context, I'll make sure the Q1 session produces something concrete enough to share externally, not just an internal plan.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Anything else from the field?

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: A few customers mentioned the enclosure gets warm to the touch after several hours of continuous logging, nothing out of spec thermally, but it surprises people.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: Might be worth a line in the user guide rather than a firmware change.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Good idea, I'll ask documentation to add a note, maybe a line about it being normal thermal behavior within spec.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Did the warmth complaint come with any actual temperature readings, or is it purely a subjective touch complaint?

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: Purely subjective as far as I've seen, nobody's reported the unit failing a thermal spec check, it's just warmer than people expect a small sensor to get.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: We could add a passive vent slot in a future enclosure revision, but that's not worth doing just for a perception issue.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Agreed, a documentation note is the right scope for now.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Anything from the general support ticket trends worth calling out, beyond the specific customer feedback?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Ticket volume's been flat month over month, but the mix has shifted a bit, we're seeing more setup and calibration questions relative to hardware failures, which honestly is a good sign, it suggests the hardware's more reliable than it used to be and the friction is now more in onboarding.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: That tracks with the sleep mode and calibration work being the right priorities, then.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Is there a specific onboarding pain point we should fix in this release versus just documentation?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I don't think it's firmware-fixable this cycle, most of it is people not understanding the calibration workflow, like when to trigger a manual recalibration versus letting the automatic drift compensation handle it.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: That's more of a user guide and maybe an in-app hint problem.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: We could surface a simple status LED pattern for "recalibration recommended" pretty cheaply, that's a small firmware change and it nudges people without them having to read anything.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: I like that, is that feasible for this release or does it need its own scoping?

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: Feasible, it's just a threshold check we already compute internally, we just haven't exposed it.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: I could have a rough version by Wednesday for Tomas to fold into the same build as the debounce fix.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: That should be easy to piggyback on, I'll leave a slot for it.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: What does the LED pattern actually look like, just so I can picture it, slow blink, color change, something else?

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: Slow amber blink, maybe once every two seconds, versus the steady green we use for normal operation.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: It's subtle enough not to alarm anyone but noticeable if you glance at the unit.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: And it clears automatically once a recalibration happens, or does someone have to acknowledge it?

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: Clears automatically, the moment the drift compensation recalculates within tolerance, no acknowledgment needed, we don't want to add a button-press requirement to something meant to reduce friction.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: That's a good design choice, adding a step would defeat the purpose.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Agreed, keep it passive.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Let's add it then, small but meaningful for the onboarding problem Maya just described.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Let's talk QA and rollout plan for a minute before we get to hardware.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: What does the test matrix look like for this release given everything we just covered?

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: I've got the regression suite running against the sleep mode changes now, that covers the standard wake, sleep, and update scenarios.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: I still need to add the three new wake-during-update cases we talked about earlier, those aren't automated yet, I've only run them manually.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Can those be automated before freeze, or do we ship with manual coverage for now?

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: I think manual is fine for this release, automating them properly means building a fixture that can interrupt a firmware update mid-flash on demand, that's a bigger project than we have time for.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: I'll write it up as a Q1 test infrastructure item instead.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Fair, add it to the Q1 list alongside the flash budget and buffer work.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Maya, what's QA coverage look like for the calibration patch specifically?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: The soak test itself is the main validation, but I'm also going to run the existing calibration regression suite against the corrected table just to make sure I haven't broken anything else in the pipeline, that's a couple hours, not a big lift.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: And the connector debounce fix, I'll have Tomas's diff go through the standard hardware-in-the-loop suite plus a manual wiggle test on the three units where we originally saw the disconnect.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Good.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: What about a broader beta rollout before general availability, or are we going straight from freeze to full release like usual?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I'd suggest a short beta window this time, maybe three days, specifically with Solenne given they're the ones who found the drift issue, so they get early confirmation it's actually fixed before we tell everyone else it's resolved.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: I like that, it closes the loop with them directly.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Can we get them opted in without much extra process?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Yeah, they're already on a beta channel from a previous engagement, I can just flip the flag on their account once the soak test passes.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Do that.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Let's also make sure support is briefed before this goes out, has anyone talked to the support team about the incoming changes?

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: Not yet, I can put together a short internal note covering the sleep mode current improvement, the calibration patch, and the connector debounce mitigation, so they're not caught flat-footed on customer calls.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Perfect, that should go out at least a couple days before general release so they have time to read it.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Anything else on QA or rollout before we move to hardware?

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Just a note that if the connector debounce fix and the calibration patch both land close together, we should stagger the release notes so customers don't think we're admitting to two unrelated defects in the same email.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Good instinct, I'll ask documentation to frame it as one consolidated Q4 update rather than a list of bugs.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Alright, now let's get to rev C hardware, since that's blocking the sleep mode current characterization.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Inès, where do things stand?

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: Boards are through fab and assembly, we're doing incoming inspection today and tomorrow.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: Barring any surprises, Tomas should have five units in hand by Friday.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: That's the same Friday you mentioned at standup this morning, right, so no slippage yet?

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: No slippage yet, I know I said the same thing last week, but the fab run actually shipped on time this time, I have the tracking number.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: What's actually changed on rev C versus rev B, remind me, since it's been a while since we scoped it?

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: Three things.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: New thermistor part, which is what fixes the calibration issue at the hardware level going forward even after this firmware patch ships.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: A revised antenna trace for slightly better BLE range.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: And a connector footprint change to address that debounce tolerance stack issue, though the debounce firmware mitigation should cover us until rev C actually ships in volume.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: So rev C is really a superset fix, firmware handles the near-term symptom and rev C handles the root cause on new units going forward.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: Exactly, and it means once rev C ships we could probably retire the debounce workaround and the corrected calibration table becomes a permanent non-issue rather than an ongoing thing we have to remember to carry forward.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: That's worth documenting somewhere so nobody removes the debounce fix prematurely, before all the rev B units are out of the field.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Good point, I'll ask Inès to note that dependency in the hardware changelog.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: What's the volume ramp look like for rev C, when do we expect it to fully replace rev B in production?

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: If incoming inspection goes clean this week, we could start mixing rev C into production runs by the end of next month, full replacement is probably a quarter out given how existing component inventory works.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Good, I'll plan to start the current draw characterization first thing Friday afternoon then, and I should have final numbers by Monday, which gives me a couple of days of buffer before the freeze.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Perfect.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Let's talk freeze and release date to close out scope.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Freeze is still the twenty-fifth, is everyone comfortable with that given what we've covered?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I'm comfortable, my soak test finishes Thursday, review Friday, patch ready well ahead of freeze.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: The only thing that would change that is if the soak test surfaces something unexpected, but twelve units in and the early data looks clean.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Comfortable, especially now that logging's deferred and rev C didn't slip.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: The recalibration LED is new scope but it's genuinely small, I'd be more worried if it were the debounce fix that grew instead.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: Comfortable from the hardware side, connector debounce fix is small and BLE diagnostic mode is already functionally done.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: Incoming inspection is the only thing that could still surprise us, but I'd have heard by now if there were a real problem with the batch.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Good, sounds like a genuinely low-risk freeze compared to some of the ones we've had, which is a nice change of pace.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Agreed, the sleep mode work last quarter was a much rockier freeze week by comparison.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Fair, I remember that one, I don't want a repeat.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Actually, sorry, one thing before we lock the date, has anyone confirmed Solenne's beta channel doesn't have any other pending changes that could confuse the drift test?

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Wait, sorry, go on.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I just want to make sure the beta build only carries the calibration fix and not, say, an early cut of the recalibration LED work too, or we won't know which change actually fixed the drift if something looks different.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Good catch.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Inès, can you confirm the beta channel branch is scoped to just the calibration patch?

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: Yes, I checked the branch config yesterday, it only pulls the calibration table change, the LED work and debounce fix are on the main release branch, not beta.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Great, that's what I wanted to hear, thank you.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Great, freeze on the twenty-fifth stands, and we're targeting general release the following Wednesday assuming QA doesn't find anything major during the freeze week.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Should we do a dry run of the release notes and internal support briefing before then, or just have them ready by the freeze date?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I'd say have a draft ready by the twenty-fifth so support has real time with it, even if it's not fully polished, better than a rushed version the day before release.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Agreed.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Who's drafting it, is that you since you're closest to the customer-facing parts, or should it be a joint effort?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I can draft the calibration and sleep mode sections, but I'd want Inès to write the connector debounce and recalibration LED parts since those are her calls to make on wording around what's a hardware issue versus a firmware mitigation.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: That works, I'll have a draft to Maya by Monday so she can merge it with her sections.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Good, and Tomas, anything customer-facing from your side that needs its own paragraph, or does it fold into Maya's calibration and sleep mode language?

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Sleep mode's covered under Maya's section I think, the battery life improvement is really the headline there regardless of who wrote which line of code.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: I don't think I need a separate paragraph.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Agreed, keep it as one coherent narrative rather than four separate engineer bios.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Let's talk resourcing for a minute, is anyone stretched thin enough that something should move to someone else?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I mentioned to you separately that I'm feeling a bit stretched between the calibration patch and catching up on everything from steerco earlier this week, but I've got help lined up, Greta and Tomas are both giving me some validation time.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Good, I saw that, thank you both for picking that up.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Anyone else?

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: I'm fine, sleep mode's basically done, the debounce fix is small, I've got room.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: Same, I'm mostly waiting on inspection results at this point, not actively blocked on anything.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Good, let's use the extra bandwidth wisely then rather than pulling forward Q1 work early, I'd rather people have slack going into freeze week than be scrambling.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: While we're on staffing, I want to flag that we may be hiring again once Aegis firmware work ramps up in Q1, does anyone have thoughts on where the team's thinnest right now?

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: Hardware validation, honestly.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: It's just me and a contractor doing incoming inspection, and that's fine at current volume, but Aegis will roughly double the board variants we're testing.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I'd agree, and I'd add that once the calibration pipeline has more people touching it, we'll want someone who can own test methodology full time rather than it being something I do alongside everything else.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Both good points, I'll factor that into the headcount conversation with Sun.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: One more thing while we're talking Aegis crossover, does the BLE diagnostic mode need any new regulatory certification given it's a new radio behavior, or does it fall under our existing approval?

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: I checked with our compliance contact last month, it falls under the existing certification since we're not changing transmit power or frequency, just adding a new data payload over the existing protocol.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: No new filing needed.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Good, one less thing to worry about for freeze.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: Right, though Aegis will likely need its own certification pass regardless, given it's a different form factor and radio module entirely, that's a Q1 conversation, not a Q4 one.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Noted, I'll make sure that's on Sun's radar too, not just ours.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Tomas, anything from the firmware side?

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: We're okay for now, sleep mode and the debounce fix are both manageable, but if Aegis needs its own firmware variant rather than sharing the Vantage codebase, that's a real second workstream, not something we absorb into current capacity.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: That's a good flag for the Q1 planning session too, whether Aegis shares the codebase or forks it, that decision affects headcount either way.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Has anyone actually looked at how much of the Vantage firmware would realistically be reusable for Aegis?

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Roughly, at a glance, the communication stack and the calibration pipeline architecture would mostly carry over, it's really the sensor driver layer and the power management specifics that would need to be rewritten for the new hardware.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: That matches what I'd guess too, calibration math is calibration math regardless of which sensor it's compensating for, it's the low-level hardware interface that changes.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: That's actually more reusable than I expected, good to know before the Q1 conversation, it might mean a fork is less necessary than Tomas was worried about a minute ago.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Fair, I was assuming more of a rewrite than there'd probably need to be, this is useful context, thanks for pushing on it.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Let's talk about the field data buffer and flash budget review Tomas mentioned, when should that happen?

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Early next week works for me, once rev C characterization is done Monday I'll have a clearer picture of headroom anyway.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Let's tentatively pencil that for Tuesday, I'll send an invite.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Anything else before we get to action items?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: One more thing, since steerco already covered the Aegis side, I want to make sure this scope makes it into my written recap to Sun, so if anything here changes between now and freeze, ping me directly rather than waiting for the next sync.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Good call.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Inès, the connector debounce issue and rev C status should probably get a line in that recap too, since Rafael was already asking about board yield at steerco.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: I'll send Maya a couple of bullet points after this.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Maya, how did the rest of steerco land overall, anything surprising come up in the room?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Mostly as expected, the one surprise was how much interest there was in the onboarding friction I mentioned earlier, Sun asked a few follow-up questions I wasn't fully prepared for.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Good thing we just scoped the LED indicator then, make sure that gets into your written recap too, sounds like it's timely for her.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Good point, I'll add it rather than wait for it to come up again next time.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Good call.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: One last logistics question, who's the point of contact for Solenne if something goes wrong during their three-day beta window?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Me, I already have a direct line to their support contact from the original drift report, it makes sense to keep continuity there rather than routing through general support.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Agreed, and if it does go wrong, what's the rollback plan?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: They'd revert to the previous firmware version, which is a standard supported downgrade path, nothing special needed.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Worst case we're back where we started, not worse off.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Good, that's the safety net I wanted to hear.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Perfect.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Okay, let's lock in action items.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: First, I'll follow up with the mobile team on the BLE diagnostic app UI timeline, that's on me, I'll have an answer by Wednesday.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Second, I'll finish the rev C current draw characterization, the connector debounce fix, and the recalibration LED indicator ahead of freeze on the twenty-fifth.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: That's a fuller plate than I had an hour ago, but none of the three pieces are large on their own.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Agreed, flag it to me directly if that combination turns out to be too much, we can always push the LED indicator to the point release if it comes to that.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Will do, I don't expect to need to, but noted.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Third, I'll finish the calibration soak test, review the results, ship the patch to Solenne Biolabs on the beta channel, and draft the calibration and sleep mode sections of the release notes, targeting early next week for the patch and Monday for the release notes draft.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: That's a lot on your plate too given the steerco recap you're also sending Sun today, are you comfortable with that stack?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I am, most of it's finishing work rather than starting from scratch, the soak test is already running and the release notes are mostly restating things we've already decided today.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: Fourth, I'll complete incoming inspection on the rev C boards, get five units to Tomas by Friday, draft the connector debounce and recalibration LED sections of the release notes for Maya by Monday, and note the rev B to rev C dependency in the hardware changelog.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: And fifth, I'll set up the Q1 planning session covering the flash budget review, the Northfield data buffer request, the cloud connectivity backoff logic, and the codebase-sharing question for Aegis firmware, aiming for that Tuesday slot we just discussed.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: That's five action items, two of them mine, which feels about right given how much you three are already carrying this cycle.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Sounds like a plan.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Agreed, this was a good one, feels like we actually have a real handle on the release now instead of a loose pile of tickets.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: Same, thanks everyone.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Thanks all, talk soon.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Thanks, I'll get that recap to Sun by end of day.

summary_markdown:
## Key decisions

- Cloud connectivity backoff logic and the twenty-four hour local data buffer increase (requested by Northfield Analytical) are deferred to a joint Q1 planning session rather than rushed into Q4, since they touch related buffer-management code.
- Firmware freeze holds at September 25th; general availability is targeted for the following Wednesday, pending a clean freeze week.
- Two small items were added to Q4 scope: a firmware-side connector debounce mitigation (masking sub-50ms USB-C disconnects) and a passive amber-LED "recalibration recommended" indicator to reduce onboarding friction.
- The corrected calibration lookup table will ship to Solenne Biolabs first, via a three-day beta window, before the wider Q4 release goes out.

## Discussion

Tomas reported the sleep-mode rewrite is functionally complete, cutting deep-sleep current from roughly 300µA to about 40µA (~7x), pending final characterization once rev C boards arrive. Maya traced the humidity-channel drift Solenne reported to a stale thermistor reference curve rather than a sensor defect; a corrected table is now in a 72-hour, three-setpoint soak test. Inès confirmed rev C hardware is through fab, with five units due to Tomas by Friday; rev C carries a new thermistor, an antenna revision, and the connector fix, meaning it addresses these issues at the hardware level going forward. The team reviewed BLE diagnostic-mode security (pairing-code gated, no sensor data exposed, no new certification required) and confirmed QA plans, including manual coverage for wake-during-update scenarios and a staged, consolidated release-notes draft due before freeze. Flash usage on the C-series is at 91%; dropping this cycle's logging work and trimming debug strings should hold it under 85% for now, with a fuller review planned for Q1.

## Action items

Five items were assigned: the owner will chase the BLE companion-app timeline with mobile and stand up the Q1 planning session; Tomas covers rev C characterization, the debounce fix, and the LED indicator; Maya finishes the soak test, ships the Solenne beta, and drafts release notes; Inès completes incoming inspection and documents the rev B/rev C dependency.

## Open questions

- Whether Aegis firmware shares the Vantage codebase or needs its own fork, and what that implies for Q1 headcount.
- Final production ramp timeline for rev C fully replacing rev B.
- Whether the flash budget will force compression work once Aegis-related code paths are shared.
